NAHHAS:v4p303/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p303/r1.claim: الرحمن begins as a nominative subject, with its predicate supplied in the following construction.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r1.claim: Raḥmān is an intensive form derived from mercy and a name whose attribute belongs uniquely to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r1.anchor: الرحمن بناء مبالغة من الرحمة، وهو اسم اختص الله تعالى بالاتصاف به،

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r1.speaker: الحسن وقطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r1.claim: They say الرحمن is a divine name people cannot appropriate for themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r1.anchor: أنه اسم ممنوع لا يستطيع الناس أن ينتحلوه ، قاله الحسن ، وقطرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r2.claim: They combine the initials الر, حم, and ن from three surahs to form one of God's names, الرحمن.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r2.anchor: فاتحة ثلاث سور إذا جمعن كن اسما من أسماء الله تعالى : { الر } و

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.speaker: Most scholars
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.claim: Most scholars consider the whole sūrah Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.anchor: all of al-Raḥmān to be a Makkan sūrah,

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.claim: A minority considers the entire sūrah Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.anchor: A minority maintain that the entire sūrah is Madinan

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r4.claim: The sūrah takes its name from al-Raḥmān, the only Divine Name directly equated with Allāh, as in 17:110.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r4.anchor: the only Divine Name to be directly equated with the Name Allāh, as in 17:110

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r5.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r5.claim: Some regard this sūrah as an extension of al-Qamar because its opening Divine Name complements the preceding sūrah's closing name.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r5.anchor: al-Raḥmān is seen by some as an extension of al-Qamar

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r6.claim: Muslims call it “The Bride of the Quran” after a well-known but unauthenticated hadith.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r6.anchor: after a well-known yet unauthenticated ḥadīth that says, “For everything there is a bride

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r7.speaker: Some commentaries
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r7.claim: Some commentaries say the sūrah answered Makkan idolaters who asked about the Prophet's frequent invocation of the Compassionate.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r7.anchor: revealed in response to the idolaters of Makkah, who are said to have asked the meaning

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r8.claim: The sūrah also recalls the idolaters' disbelief in the Compassionate, noted in 13:30.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r8.anchor: The idolaters’ disbelief in the Compassionate is also mentioned in 13:30

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r9.claim: Verses 1–25 present God as Creator, Teacher, and Revealer and describe blessings in the created world; the sūrah then turns to heavenly blessings.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r9.anchor: The first section of the sūrah (vv. 1–25) discusses the nature of the Compassionate as Creator, Teacher, and Revealer

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.claim: God's enduring reality offsets the dualities: verses 26–27 stress that God remains while everything else passes away.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.anchor: vv. 26–27, which emphasize that God remains while all else fades away

TABRISI:55:1-13/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r3.claim: Al-Raḥmān denotes the One whose mercy encompasses everything and is reserved for God; raḥim and raḥīm may also describe people.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r3.anchor: الرحمن هو الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء فلذلك لا يوصف به إلا الله تعالى

TABRISI:55:1-13/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r6.claim: Al-Raḥmān is elliptical for “God, the Merciful,” so it can stand as a verse and preserve the verse-ending pattern.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r6.anchor: الرحمن آية مع أنه ليس بجملة لأنه في تقدير الله الرحمن

TABRISI:55:1-13/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r9.claim: The name answers Meccans who asked who the Merciful was after being told to worship Him.

TABRISI:55:1-13/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r10.claim: When told to call upon God or the Merciful, Meccans denied knowing the latter name; revelation clarifies who al-Raḥmān is.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r10.anchor: قالوا: ما نعرف الرحمن إلا صاحب اليمامة فقيل لهم الرحمن

ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r1.claim: Most commentators classify the surah as Meccan, while Zamakhshari and Suyuti assign it to Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r1.anchor: regard this surah as a Meccan revelation, Zamakhshari and (among the later scholars) Suyuti ascribe it to the Medina period

ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r2.speaker: Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r2.claim: Baydawi leaves the period open and allows that portions may precede and follow the Prophet's emigration to Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r2.anchor: question open, and adds that parts of it may

ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r3.claim: Some authorities place it just after surah 13, but Asad finds this unhelpful because surah 13 also cannot be dated confidently.
ASAD-NOTES:55:intro/r3.anchor: Some authorities are of the opinion that it followed immediately upon surah 13 ("Thunder"): an opinion which is not very helpful

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r3.claim: Rahman names God as the one whose mercy and beneficence are boundless and continually joined; Elmalılı refers readers to his earlier explanation in the Fatiha commentary.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r3.anchor: nâmütenâhî kaynaşıp duran ve ondan dolayı bir ismi de Rahmân olan Allah teâlâ

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r4.claim: Although Rahman appears grammatically as a subject followed by its predicate, its status as a separate verse permits reading it as the predicate of an omitted subject: God is Rahman.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r4.anchor: İ‘rabca zâhir olan mübtedâ, mâba‘di haber görünür. Lâkin müstakil bir âyet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.claim: Some classify Sūrah al-Raḥmān as Madinan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.anchor: Some people have regarded this sūrah to be Madīnan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.claim: The author rejects a Madinan classification, arguing that no verse appears to be Madinan and the whole sūrah shares one tone and rhythm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.anchor: a single verse of it appears to be Mad īnan much less the whole sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.claim: The sūrah’s Makkan opponents demand a punishment sign before accepting that rejection brings punishment and everlasting humiliation in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.anchor: his opponents, in their fury to refute him, had become adamant on a demand: unless a sign of punishment was shown to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.claim: The preceding Sūrah al-Qamar taught Quraysh to learn from messengers and their history rather than insist on seeing punishment; revelation itself is a favor for education and remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.anchor: In Sūrah al-Qamar, the obdurate people of the Quraysh were told to learn a lesson from messengers and the history of their people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.claim: God taught the Qur’an out of mercy; granting speech means humans can understand and teach one another, so they should use this exalted ability for instruction rather than punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.anchor: It is the merciful nature of the Almighty because of which He has taught them the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.claim: The sūrah opens by presenting the Qur’an as divine mercy and teaching; human creation and speech make people fit to learn through revelation rather than punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.anchor: The sūrah begins with the declaration that the Qur’ ān is a manifestation of the graciousness of the Almighty.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r2.claim: Most say the surah is Meccan; Ibn Masʿud says Medinan. Ibn Abbas reports both and says verse 29 is a Medinan exception in one account.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r2.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور، مدنية في قول ابن مسعود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.claim: He says the surah followed people's refusal to prostrate to الرحمن because they did not know the name, prompting الرحمن علم القرآن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.anchor: وسبب نزولها فيما قال مقاتل: أنه لما نزل وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن الآية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r5.claim: Another view says it was revealed in Medina when Suhayl ibn ʿAmr and others refused to write the basmala in the treaty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r5.anchor: وقيل: مدنية نزلت، إذ أبى سهيل بن عمرو وغيره أن يكتب في الصلح:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r6.claim: After the preceding surah briefly names the righteous' abode with the mighty King, this surah details divine signs and expands both groups' destinations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r6.anchor: ومناسبة هذه السورة لما قبلها: أنه لما ذكر مقر المتقين في جنات ونهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.claim: Teaching the Qur'an is an effect of mercy and heals hearts; الرحمن is apparently the subject and علم القرآن its predicate, though another parse supplies an omitted predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.anchor: الرحمن، علم القرآن، فذكر ما نشأ عن صفة الرحمة،

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish God’s universal mercy, inviting hope in His gifts and warning that He may end further favor through punishment; it does so by recounting creation’s wonders and blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r1.anchor: فمقصودها بالذات إثبات الاتصاف بعموم الرحمة ترغيبا في إنعامه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r2.claim: The title ‘Bride of the Qur’an’ evokes its gathering of adornments, garments, jewels, crowns, blessings, beauty, and perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r2.anchor: لأنها الحاوية لما فيه من حلى وحلل ، وجواهر وكلل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r3.claim: The basmala describes God’s perfection as shown in creation, universal mercy in wondrous works and signs, and special mercy to the obedient through worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370#s055/r3.anchor: الذي ظهر عموم رحمته بما بهر من بدائع مصنوعاته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.claim: After the preceding surah’s emphasis on sovereignty and power, this surah counts blessings in both worlds; universal mercy completes kingship, and its opening name signals that theme.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.anchor: قصر هذه السورة على تعداد نعمه على خلقه في الدارين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r3.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r3.claim: Ibn Burjān describes the name al-Raḥmān as the manifest aspect of the name Allah and the hidden aspect of the name al-Rabb; the three names disclose and veil the divine essence to creatures.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r3.anchor: قال ابن برجان : وهو ظاهر اسمه الله , وباطن اسمه الرب

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.claim: The surah opens with al-Rahman to express God's immense mercy and blessings for all servants, while religion is the greatest gift to rational beings and the Qur'an its highest gift to humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.anchor: Sûreye Cenâb-ı Allah’ın rahmetinin enginliğini, kulluk görevini yapsın yapmasın bütün kullarına nimet vermesini ifade eden Rahmân ismiyle ve O’nun Kur’an’ı öğretmesiyle başlanmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.claim: Some exegetes take the verb usually meaning “taught” as “made a sign”: God made the Qur'an a miracle proving Muhammad's prophethood and containing signs for reflective readers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.anchor: “Öğretti” anlamına gelen fiile “alâmet kıldı” mânası da verilebildiğinden bazı müfessirler bu âyetler için şöyle bir yorum yapmışlardır

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r1.claim: The surah is called the Bride of the Quran; the source gives differing reports about whether it is Meccan or Medinan and about its verse count.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r1.anchor: وتسمى عروس القرآن مكية أو مدنية وآيها ست أو سبع أو ثمان وسبعون

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r2.claim: “The All-Merciful” begins the sentence and means the One whose mercy is complete; worldly provision is general, while forgiveness in the afterlife is granted to believers.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r2.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ما بعده أي الذي له الرحمة الكاملة

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r3.claim: A Persian poem depicts the earth as God's common table, where friend and enemy alike share its bounty.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r3.anchor: أديم زمين سفره عام اوست برين خوان يغما ه دشمن ه دوست

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r4.claim: Mercy in creatures is affection or spiritual inclination, named by analogy with the womb's physical bending over what it carries; for God it means willing good or bestowing favor.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r4.anchor: وأريد بها بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى إرادة الخير أو الإنعام

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r5.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r5.claim: Al-Ghazālī describes the Merciful as caring for servants through creation, guidance to faith and happiness, their afterlife joy, and the gift of seeing the divine face.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r5.anchor: الرحمن هو العطوف على العباد بالإيجاد أولا وبالهداية إلى الإيمان وأسباب السعادة ثانيا

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r6.claim: Because the surah counts worldly and otherworldly, bodily and spiritual blessings, it opens with the name Rahman, the name of the essence encompassing all names and attributes, to ascribe those gifts to Him.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r6.anchor: شاملة لتعداد النعم الدنيوية والأخروية والجسمانية والروحانية طرزها بطراز اسم الرحمن

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r7.claim: The Quran is the greatest blessing and the basis of all happiness; the cited saying calls Quran-bearers the community's noblest, meaning those who regularly recite it and keep night vigils.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r7.anchor: لأنه مدار جميع السعادات ولذا قال عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r8.claim: The Prophet also says the best people learn the Quran and teach it; it contains the realities of all heavenly scriptures, and its teaching flows from broad divine mercy.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r8.anchor: خيركم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه وفيه جميع حقائق الكتب السماوية

QASHANI:55:1-2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:1-2/r1.claim: “The All-Merciful” names God as the giver, at the beginning, of all foundational blessings: entities and their first perfections; its broad scope grounds the attributes that follow.
QASHANI:55:1-2/r1.anchor: اسم خاص من أسماء الله تعالى باعتبار إفاضة أصول النعم كلها من الأعيان وكمالاتها الأولية بحسب البداية

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r1.claim: The basmala announces God's might and greatness as well as His bounty and mercy; witnessing majesty completes the spirits' joy and experiencing mercy brings bodily bliss, for majesty makes Him worshiped and mercy makes Him loved.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r1.claim: One report says the opening name al-Raḥmān was revealed when people asked who the Merciful was.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r1.anchor: قيل: نزلت حين قالوا: وما الرحمن؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r2.claim: Another report takes al-Raḥmān as an answer to Meccans who claimed a human taught the Prophet.

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r2.claim: Because the sūrah enumerates worldly and otherworldly blessings, it opens with the name al-Raḥmān.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r2.anchor: لما كانت السورة مقصورة على تعداد النعم الدنيوية والآخروية صدرها ب { الرحمن }

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.claim: They compare God's teaching all names to angels with His teaching Muhammad the Qur'an, which He presents to Himself; the disputing high assembly means the angels.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : علم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة وعلم محمدا القرآن وعرضه على نفسه فقال : فيما يختصم الملأ الأعلى يعني الملائكة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.claim: The Qur'an is the greatest blessing, the summit and foundation of the heavenly books, clarifying what pleases God and what must be avoided; it leads to the promised abode.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.anchor: أجل النعم نعمة ادين التي تتبعها نعمة الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.claim: Jaʿfar says the whole Qur'an is miraculous and its arrangement overpowers opponents, while some passages disclose its eloquence more immediately; he points to Sūrat al-Qamar's concise stories that still complete their aims and admonitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام جعفر بن الزبير : من المعلوم أن الكتاب العزيز وإن كانت آية كلها معجزة باهرة وسورة في جليل النظم وبديع التأليف قاطعة بالخصوم قاهرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.claim: The commentary gives the address to earth and sky and the command to proclaim as examples of instantly evident Qur'anic eloquence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.anchor: { وقيل يا أرض ابتلغي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي } [ هود : 44 ]

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r4.claim: The name al-Raḥmān signals God's mercy and immense beneficence through the Qur'an, whose blessings cannot be enumerated.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r4.anchor: وخص من أسمائه الحسنى هذاالاسم إشعارا برحمته بالكتاب وعظيم إحسانه به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.claim: Sūrat al-Raḥmān follows al-Qamar to address both humans and jinn, establish proof for both kinds, and repeatedly remind them of God's favors.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.anchor: فاتبعت سورة القمر بسورة الرحمن تنبيها للثقلين وإعذارا إليهم وتقريرا للجنسين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.claim: Al-Rāzī says the closing Name refers back to the opening Name of the sūrah, encompassing both Qur'anic teaching and divine punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : كأنه يريد بالاسم الذي افتتح به السورة وقد انعطف آخر السورة على أولها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p105/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p105/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p105/r1.claim: When Meccan unbelievers rejected the name al-Rahman after 25:60 was revealed, God identified the rejected al-Rahman as the one who taught the Quran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p105/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل لما نزل قوله اسجدوا للرحمن الفرقان 60 قال كفار مكة وما الرحمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Surah al-Rahman as Meccan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r1.anchor: وهي مكية. قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا عفان،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the Prophet paired the opening surahs of the Mufassal two by two; in his arrangement, al-Rahman began the Mufassal.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r3.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r3.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet recited all of al-Rahman to his companions; they were silent, and the Prophet recalled the jinn's better response to its repeated refrain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r3.anchor: عن جابر قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أصحابه فقرأ عليهم سورة "الرحمن" من أولها إلى آخرها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r4.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Jabir report gharīb, known only through al-Walid ibn Muslim from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r4.anchor: ثم قال: هذا حديث غريب، لا نعرفه إلا من حديث الوليد بن مسلم، عن زهير بن محمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r5.speaker: أحمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r5.claim: Ahmad did not recognize the report and objected to Syrian transmitters narrating it from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r5.anchor: ثم حكى عن الإمام أحمد أنه كان لا يعرفه، ينكر (3) رواية أهل الشام عن زهير بن محمد هذا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r6.speaker: البزار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r6.claim: Al-Bazzar says the Jabir narration is known only by this route through al-Walid ibn Muslim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r6.anchor: ثم قال: لا نعرفه يروى إلا من هذا الوجه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r7.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet read al-Rahman, or it was read in his presence, and remarked on the jinn's better response.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ سورة "الرحمن" -أو: قرئت عنده-فقال: "ما لي أسمع الجن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r8.speaker: البزار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r8.claim: Al-Bazzar says the Ibn Umar hadith is known from the Prophet only through this chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p488/r8.anchor: ثم قال: لا نعلمه يروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا من هذا الوجه بهذا الإسناد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.claim: God's favor and mercy include sending the Quran to His servants and making its memorization and understanding easy for those He shows mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن فضله ورحمته بخلقه: أنه أنزل على عباده القرآن ويسر حفظه وفهمه على من رحمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.claim: Zamakhsharī places the Quran first among divine favors because religion is the foremost favor; its revelation and teaching are the highest-ranked revelation and the summit, proof, and standard of heavenly books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.anchor: وهي نعمة الدين ، فقدم من نعمة الدين ما هو في أعلى مراتبها وأقصى مراقيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.claim: Mentioning human creation after the Quran shows that humanity was created for religion and to know revelation and scripture; the purpose of human creation is presented as prior to creation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.anchor: وأخر ذكر خلق الإنسان عن ذكره ، ثم أتبعه إياه : ليعلم أنه إنما خلقه للدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.claim: Al-Raḥmān is the subject; the following verbs with their pronouns form successive predicates without conjunctions, matching a listing of favors and making each clause an independent rebuke to deniers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.anchor: أخبار مترادفة ، وإخلاؤها من العاطف لمجيئها على نمط التعديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.claim: He illustrates the rebuke by listing how Zayd was helped after poverty, lowliness, and scarcity, then asking what kindness he could deny.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.anchor: زيد أغناك بعد فقر ، أعزك بعد ذل ، كثرك بعد قلة ، فعل بك ما لم يفعل أحد بأحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.claim: The first clauses omit conjunctions so each independently rebukes deniers by enumerating benefactions; conjunctions resume for clauses that suit and approach each other.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.anchor: ثم رد الكلام إلى منهاجه بعد التبكيت في وصل ما يجب وصله للتناسب والتقارب بالعاطف

MUQATIL:55:1-4/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r1.claim: When Meccan polytheists were told to prostrate to al-Rahman, they denied knowing that name; God identifies Himself and recounts His works so people may know and worship Him alone.
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r1.anchor: فأكروا الرحمن، وقالوا: لا نعرف الرحمن، فأخبر الله تعالى عن نفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.claim: The word al-insan in the creation verse may mean humanity as a kind, Adam, or Muhammad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ الرحمن علم القرآن خلق الإنسان ﴾ اى الجنس أو آدم أو محمدا عليهما السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī take the opening as the combined initials alif-lām-rāʾ, ḥā-mīm, and nūn, forming one of God’s names, al-Raḥmān.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وعامر الشعبي: { الرحمن } فاتحة ثلاث سور إذا جمعن كن اسما من أسماء الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r1.claim: The opening contrasts the prior surah’s display of majesty through the moon’s splitting with this surah’s merciful miracle, the Qur’an that purifies hearts of sins.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r1.anchor: افتتح السورة المتقدمة بذكر معجزة تدل على العزة والجبروت والهيبة وهو انشقاق القمر

RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r2.claim: The prior surah repeatedly recalls punishment, while this surah repeatedly recalls divine favors, matching their respective emphasis on awe and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r2.anchor: ذكر في السورة المتقدمة : { فكيف كان عذابى ونذر } ( القمر : 16 ) غير مرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r3.claim: The repeated refrain about divine favors completes the contrast with the prior surah’s repeated warning about punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r3.anchor: وذكر في السورة : { فبأى ءالاء ربكما تكذبان } ( الرحمن : 13 ) مرة بعد مرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r4.claim: The ending of al-Qamar, ‘with a Sovereign, Powerful,’ leads into al-Rahman: power signals majesty, while this opening gathers divine might toward disbelievers and mercy toward the righteous.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r4.anchor: عند مليك مقتدر } ( القمر : 55 ) ، والاقتدار إشارة إلى الهيبة والعظمة

RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r5.claim: ‘The All-Merciful’ describes God as mighty, avenging, and powerful toward disbelievers and wicked people, but as merciful, beneficent, and forgiving toward the righteous.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73/r5.anchor: أي عزيز شديد منتقم مقتدر بالنسبة إلى الكفار والفجار ، رحمن منعم غافر للأبرار

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r1.claim: Some treat Allah, and some also al-Rahman, as proper names; they cite the permission to invoke either name and allow the vocative ‘O All-Merciful.’
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r1.anchor: من الناس من يقول : إن الله مع الألف واللام اسم علم لموجد الممكنات وعلى هذا فمنهم من قال : { الرحمان } أيضا اسم علم

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi rejects those proper-name claims as weak, especially the vocative ‘O All-Merciful.’
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r2.anchor: وجوز بعضهم قول القائل : يا الرحمن كما يجوز يا الله وتمسك بالآية وكل هذا ضعيف وبعضها أضعف من بعض

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r3.claim: Allah is unlikely to be a proper name with the article because its initial hamza would then be radical and could not drop as a hamzat waṣl in forms such as ‘creation of Allah.’
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r3.anchor: لو كان كذلك لكانت الهمزة فيه أصلية ، فلا يجوز أن تجعل وصلية ، وكان يجب أن يقال : خلق الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r4.claim: A sound alternative makes Ilāh or Lāh the proper name for the creator, with the article later attached as in other personal names.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r4.anchor: الحق فيه أحد القولين : إما أن نقول : إله أو لاه اسم لموجد الممكنات اسم علم ، ثم استعمل مع الألف واللام

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r5.claim: On the proper-name analysis, God’s sovereign reservation of a name makes idolaters’ naming idols with it transgressive, even if language alone permits the usage.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r5.anchor: والله تعالى ملك مطاع وكل من عداه تحت أمره فإذا استأثر لنفسه اسما لا يجوز للعبيد أن يتسموا بذلك الاسم

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, Ilāh or Lāh means ‘the one worshipped’; because that meaning belongs only to God, the definite name cannot be given to another, even a son, lest it imply the meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r6.anchor: إله أو لاه اسم لمن يعبد والألف واللام للتعريف ، ولما امتنع المعنى عن غير الله امتنع الاسم

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r7.claim: Names such as al-Karim and al-Wadud are permissible because their meanings may also be intended, whereas al-Khaliq, al-Qadim, and ‘the worshipped’ cannot be given to people.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r7.anchor: فيجوز تسمية الواحد بالكريم والودود ولا يجوز تسميته بالخالق ، والقديم لأن على تقدير حمله على أنه علم غير ملحوظ فيه المعنى يجوز

RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r8.claim: Given this analysis of Allah, treating al-Rahman as a proper name is even less defensible, and permitting ‘O All-Merciful’ is weakest of all.
RAZI-FULL:v29p73#2/r8.anchor: فما يترتب عليه ، وهو أن الرحمن اسم على أضعف منه ، وتجويز يا الرحمن أضعف من الكل

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r1.claim: Al-Rahman functions like an original name paired with a dominant epithet that became name-like through frequent use, but it is exclusive to God.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r1.anchor: الله والرحمن في حق الله تعالى كالاسم الأول والوصف الغالب الذي يصير كالاسم بعد الاسم الأول

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r2.claim: Calling the Yamami man al-Rahman is a linguistic possibility used transgressively, like calling another being ‘a god,’ and rests on false belief.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r2.anchor: من الناس من أطلق لفظ الرحمن على اليمامي ، نقول : هو كما أن من الناس من أطلق لفظ الإله على غير الله تعديا وكفرا

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r3.claim: God has prior mercy in creating beings and later mercy in sustaining them with provision, understanding, and aid; hence He is al-Rahman for the first and al-Rahim for the latter.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r3.anchor: لله تعالى رحمتان سابقة ولاحقة فالسابقة هي التي بها خلق الخلق واللاحقة هي التي أعطى بها الخلق بعد إيجاده إياهم من الرزق والفطنة

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r4.claim: No one else may be called al-Rahman because no other being creates; people may be called rahim insofar as they imitate later mercy by feeding, clothing, and helping others.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r4.anchor: فلما لم يوجد في غيره هذه الرحمة ولم يخلق أحد حدا لم يجز أن يقال لغيره : رحمن

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r5.claim: Grammatically, al-Rahman is the subject whose predicate is the verbal sentence ‘He taught the Qur’an’; this is the sounder analysis.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r5.anchor: { الرحمان } مبتدأ خبره الجملة الفعلية التي هي قوله : { علم القرءان }

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r6.claim: A weaker parse makes al-Rahman the predicate of an omitted ‘He is,’ and treats it as a standalone verse.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r6.anchor: وقيل { الرحمان } ( خبر ) مبتدأ تقديره هو الرحمن ، ثم أتى بجملة بعد جملة

RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r7.claim: Al-Razi prefers the first grammatical analysis; the second depends on the weaker standalone-verse reading.
RAZI-FULL:v29p74/r7.anchor: والأول أصح ، وعلى القول الضعيف الرحمن آية

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r1.claim: One analysis reads ‘taught’ as ‘made it a sign’: the Qur’an is a prophetic sign and miracle, parallel to the moon-splitting miracle, through its unique knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r1.anchor: قيل : علم بمعنى جعله علامة أي هو علامة النبوة ومعجزة

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r2.claim: Alternatively, God made the Qur’an learnable, as in ‘We made the Qur’an easy for remembrance’; teaching here is metaphorical, as when one funds a learner’s instruction.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r2.anchor: أنه جعله بحيث يعلم فهو كقوله : { ولقد يسرنا القرءان للذكر } ( القمر : 17 ) والتعليم على هذا الوجه مجاز

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r3.claim: The omitted second object may be Gabriel and other angels: God taught them the Qur’an and then sent it down to His servant.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r3.anchor: المفعول الثاني لا بد منه وهو جبريل وغيره من الملائكة علمهم القرآن ثم أنزله على عبده

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r4.claim: Another possible second object is Muhammad, emphasizing that the Qur’an is God’s speech rather than Muhammad’s.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال : المفعول الثاني هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وفيه إشارة إلى أن القرآن كلام الله تعالى لا كلام محمد

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r5.claim: A third reading makes humanity the recipient; al-Razi says this best completes the blessing because the surah begins by enumerating universal favors.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r5.anchor: وفيه وجه ثالث : وهو أنه تعالى علم القرآن الإنسان ، وهذا أقرب ليكون الإنعام أتم

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r6.claim: The second object is omitted to stress that teaching is a universal favor, not instruction given only to one person, as in the general statement that someone feeds people.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى أن النعمة في تعميم التعليم لا في تعليم شخص دون شخص

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r7.claim: Teaching means imparting knowledge; the statement does not conflict with 3:7, whether the learned are joined to God or treated as a separate clause that can learn difficult passages within human capacity.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r7.anchor: من علم كتابا عظيما ووقع على ما فيه ، وفيه مواضع مشكلة فعلم ما في تلك المواضع بقدر الإمكان

RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r8.claim: On a reading that stops at ‘except God,’ no one independently discovers the Qur’an’s interpretation through intellect; people know only what God teaches them.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75/r8.anchor: لا يعلم تأويله إلا الله وأما غيره فلا يعلم من تلقاء نفسه مالم يعلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.claim: If Qur’an teaching means teaching angels, God taught them before creating humans; the preserved Qur’an is touched only by the purified and then sent down from the Lord of the worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.anchor: فعلم تعالى ملائكته المقربين القرآن حقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.claim: This order pairs celestial matters with earthly ones and names the celestial first: Qur’an teaching above is paired with teaching expression to humans below.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.anchor: ذكر أمورا علوية وأمورا سفلية ، وكل علوي قابله بسفلي ، وقدم العلويات على السفليات

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.claim: The sun and moon among celestial signs are paired with the stars and trees prostrating among earthly signs.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.anchor: وقال : { الشمس والقمر } ( القيامة : 9 ) في العلويات وقال في مقابلتهما من السفليات : { والنجم والشجر يسجدان } ( الرحمن : 6 )

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.claim: The raised heaven is paired with the placed earth, continuing the sequence of celestial signs before earthly ones.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.anchor: والسماء رفعها } ( الرحمن : 7 ) وفي مقابلتها : { والارض وضعها } ( الرحمن : 10 )

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, Qur’an teaching comes first because it is the greatest favor; ‘created humanity, taught him expression’ then explains how that teaching is given.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.anchor: تقديم تعليم القرآن إشارة إلى كونه أتم نعمة وأعظم إنعاما

STUDYQURAN:55:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r1.claim: Al-Raḥmān denotes unqualified, boundless mercy prior to creation; it is also rendered “the Infinitely Good” or “the Loving.”
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r1.anchor: al-Raḥmān, which is considered to denote that aspect of mercy and compassion that is unqualified, boundless, and prior to the created order.

STUDYQURAN:55:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r2.claim: Al-Raḥmān is uniquely divine because existence is made manifest through this Name as a universal mercy that cannot be attributed to another.
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r2.anchor: one of the Divine Names that can only apply to God, for it is one of the Names by which existence itself is made manifest

STUDYQURAN:55:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r3.speaker: Sufis
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r3.claim: Many Sufis say that all creation is brought forth through the Breath of the Compassionate.
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r3.anchor: many Sufis say that all of creation is brought forth through “the Breath of the Compassionate.”

STUDYQURAN:55:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r4.claim: Al-Raḥīm denotes more particular Divine mercy and can describe humans; al-Raḥmān relates to the Essence, while al-Raḥīm refers to mercy extended through God's acts.
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r4.anchor: a more particular form of Divine Mercy and by which human beings may also be described.

STUDYQURAN:55:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r5.claim: Al-Raḥmān relates more directly to the Divine Essence, while al-Raḥīm refers to God's mercy extended in all acts.
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r5.anchor: al-Raḥmān relates more directly to the Divine Essence, while al-Raḥīm can be seen as referring to the extension of God’s Mercy in all acts

STUDYQURAN:55:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r6.claim: The Compassionate is said to assume God's Throne.
STUDYQURAN:55:1/r6.anchor: the Compassionate who is said to assume the Throne of God in 20:5 (cf. 25:59).

SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r1.claim: For those counting al-Rahman as a verse together with an implied element, it can be the predicate of an unspoken subject: “God is al-Rahman.”
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه خبر مبتدأ مضمر، أي: الله الرحمن.

SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r2.claim: Alternatively, for the same verse-counting view, al-Rahman can be the subject with an omitted predicate: “Al-Rahman is our Lord.”
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه مبتدأ، وخبره مضمر، أي: الرحمن ربنا.

SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r3.claim: A third analysis does not count al-Rahman as a verse by itself; it begins one clause with what follows, with “taught the Quran” as its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:55:1/r3.anchor: الثالث أنه ليس بآية، وأنه مع ما بعده كلام واحد، وهو مبتدأ خبره " علم القرآن ".

ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r1.claim: Al-Raḥmān is a name exclusive to God, found in earlier scriptures, meaning abundant in mercy.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r1.anchor: الرحمن) اسم من أسماء الله تعالى. لا يقال لغيره، وهو في الكتب المتقدمة، ومعناه الكثير الرحمة.

THALABI:v9p177#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#2/r1.claim: One reported occasion for the opening is that people asked, “What is the All-Merciful?”
THALABI:v9p177#2/r1.anchor: الرحمن علم القرآن نزلت حين قالوا: وما الرحمن؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.claim: When 17:110 was revealed, Meccan disbelievers said they knew only Musaylima, the Rahman of al-Yamama; 25:60 records their denial of the name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.anchor: قال كفار مكة: ما نعرف إلا مسيلمة، رحمان اليمامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.claim: God identifies himself by mentioning his works so that people will recognize him and affirm his oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.anchor: فأخبر الله عن نفسه، وذكر صنعه ليعرف فيوحد

BURHAN:v1p245/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p245/r3.speaker: ابن السيد
BURHAN:v1p245/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid says the ninth division begins with al-Raḥmān and attributes that arrangement to Ibn Masʿūd's codex; al-Zarkashī says Aḥmad likewise transmits it.
BURHAN:v1p245/r3.anchor: ﴿ الرحمن ﴾ حكاه ابن السيد فى أماليه على الموطأ

ITQAN:v1p43/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p43/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p43/r6.claim: Suyūṭī holds that the majority correctly classify al-Raḥmān as Meccan; al-Tirmidhī and al-Ḥākim report that the jinn responded to the refrain more warmly than the Companions, and al-Ḥākim grades the report sound on the two Shaykhs’ condition.
ITQAN:v1p43/r6.anchor: سورة الرحمن الجمهور على أنها مكية وهو الصواب ويدل له ما رواه الترمذي والحاكم عن جابر قال لما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v1p43/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p43/r7.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
ITQAN:v1p43/r7.claim: A good-chain report from Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr says she heard the Prophet reciting al-Raḥmān near the Kaʿba corner before public proclamation while the polytheists listened; this more clearly shows it preceded al-Ḥijr.
ITQAN:v1p43/r7.anchor: وأصرح منه في الدلالة ما أخرجه أحمد في مسنده بسند جيد عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت سمعت رسول الله

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.claim: An unnamed scholar proposes that repeating the relative and locative phrase specifies individuals; a single relative instead signals the general class and foregrounds the verse's main purpose, as in al-Raḥmān.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أنه تأمل ما في التنزيل العزيز من قوله تعالى: (من في السماوات والأرض) و: (من في السماوات ومن في الأرض)

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r1.claim: One reported occasion is the polytheists' question What is the All-Merciful?; the sura's title then affirms the divine attribute they denied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r1.anchor: وقد قيل : إن سبب نزولها قول المشركين المحكي في قول تعالى :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r2.speaker: جمهور الصحابة والتابعين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r2.claim: The majority of the Companions and Successors classify the sura as Meccan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r2.anchor: وهي مكية في قول جمهور الصحابة والتابعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to call the sura Medinan, revealed during the Hudaybiyya treaty when Suhayl ibn Amr refused to write the basmala.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r3.anchor: روى جماعة عن ابن عباس : أنها مدنية نزلت في صلح القضية عندما أبى سهيل بن عمرو أن يكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r4.claim: A Medinan classification is also attributed to Ibn Masud.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r4.anchor: ونسب إلى ابن مسعود أيضا أنها مدنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers that the entire sura is Meccan; Ibn Masud's codex places it at the start of the mufassal section.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r6.anchor: والأصح أنها مكية كلها ، وهي في مصحف ابن مسعود أول المفصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r7.claim: If the occasion was the polytheists' denial of the name al-Rahman, the sura followed al-Furqan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r7.anchor: وإذا صح أن سبب نزولها قول المشركين { وما الرحمن تكون نزلت بعد سورة الفرقان .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r9.claim: The sura is among the earliest revelations; a report of the Prophet reciting it before public preaching places it before al-Hijr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r9.anchor: وهي من أول السور نزولا فقد أخرج أحمد في مسنده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r11.claim: The disagreement over whether the sura is Meccan or Medinan prevents a firm placement in the revelation chronology.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r11.anchor: وللاختلاف فيها لم تحقق رتبتها في عداد نزول سور القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r12.speaker: الجعبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r12.claim: Al-Ja'bari ranks it ninety-eighth on the Medinan view, after al-Ra'd and before al-Insan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r12.anchor: وعدها الجعبري ثامنة وتسعين بناء على القول بأنها مدنية وجعلها بعد سورة الرعد وقبل سورة الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r13.claim: On the preferred Meccan chronology, he places it forty-third, after al-Furqan and before Fatir, and before al-Hijr and al-Nahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r13.anchor: فالوجه أن تعد ثالثة وأربعين بعد سورة الفرقان وقبل سورة فاطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r14.claim: Medina and Mecca count seventy-seven verses, Syria and Kufa seventy-eight, and Basra seventy-six; the difference comes from counting al-Rahman itself as a verse in Kufa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r14.anchor: وعد أهل المدينة ومكة آيها سبعا وسبعين ، وأهل الشام والكوفة ثمانيا وسبعين لأنهم عدوا الرحمن آية ، وأهل البصرة ستا وسبعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.claim: The Kashshaf says the sura leads with the greatest religious favor, Quranic revelation and teaching, then human creation and the distinctive gift of expression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( أراد الله أن يقدم في عدد آلائه أول شيء ما هو أسبق قدما من ضروب آلائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r8.claim: The striking opening with al-Rahman is unique: no other sura begins directly with a divine name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r8.anchor: ومن بديع أسلوبها افتتاحها الباهر باسمه { الرحمن } وهي السورة الوحيدة المفتتحة باسم من أسماء الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.claim: Most verse counters treat the opening as one verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.anchor: هذه آية واحدة عند جمهور العادين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r11.claim: Hafs copies mark an ayah after al-Rahman because the Kufa readers count that name as a verse, producing their total of seventy-eight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r11.anchor: ووقع في المصاحف التي برواية حفص عن عاصم علامة آية عقب كلمة { الرحمن } ، إذ عدها قراء الكوفة آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r12.claim: If al-Rahman is a separate verse, it can be a predicate of an omitted subject, understood as He is al-Rahman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r12.anchor: فإذا جعل اسم { الرحمن } آية تعين أن يكون اسم ( الرحمن ) : إما خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف تقديره : هو الرحمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r13.claim: Alternatively, al-Rahman can be the subject with a predicate omitted according to the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r13.anchor: أو مبتدأ خبره محذوف يقدر بما يناسب المقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r14.claim: Alternatively the name is mentioned as a word to expose the pagans' error in denying it, like the isolated letters at sura openings; this is Ibn Ashur's strongest account of those letters and a rebuke to the deniers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون واقعا موقع الكلمات التي يراد لفظها للتنبيه على غلط المشركين إذ أنكروا هذا الاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r6.claim: The name al-Rahman suits these favors through the description of the Prophet as mercy to all worlds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r6.anchor: ومناسبة اسم { الرحمن } لهذه الاعتبارات منتزعة من قوله : { وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين }

IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.claim: ʿUrwa reports that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was the first after the Prophet to recite the Qurʾān publicly in Mecca; Quraysh beat him as he continued, but he returned ready to repeat it.
IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: كان أول من جهر بالقرآن بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة عبد الله بن مسعود

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r4.claim: Al-Rahman aims to establish God’s universal mercy, shown by his knowledge and power in creation’s wonders, recalling blessings to encourage gratitude and warn of the loss of further favor through vengeance.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r4.anchor: مقصودها بالذات إثبات الاتصاف بعموم الرحمة ترغيبا في إنعامه وإحسانه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r5.claim: The title ‘Bride of the Qur’an’ says the surah gathers the Qur’an’s adornments, beauties, jewels, and crowns.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r5.anchor: واسمها عروس القرآن واضح البيان في ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r6.claim: In the basmala, Allah’s name points to the encompassing perfection made visible in the marvels of creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r6.anchor: الذي ظهرت إحاطة كماله بما ظهر من عجائب مخلوقاته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r7.claim: In the basmala, al-Rahman’s universal mercy appears through the wonders of creation and signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r7.anchor: الذي ظهر عموم رحمته بما بهر من بدائع مصنوعاته واشتهر من عظيم آياته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r8.claim: In the basmala, al-Rahim singles out the obedient, whose humility through worship brings them honor and God’s approval.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p370/r8.anchor: الذي ظهر اختصتصه لأهل طاعته بما تحققوا به من الذل المفيد للعز بلزوم عباداته
